Opinion of the Judge : Accused found not guilty.

(GIRISH CHATNI)
 XXIX ACJM, BENGALURU  JUDGMENT The P.S.I., of Kothanuru Police Station, Bengaluru, has filed the present charge sheet against the accused for the C.C.No.60156/2018 offence punishable under sections 289, 506 of Indian Penal Code.

2. BRIEF FACTS OF THE PROSECUTION CASE ARE AS UNDER :
It is the case of the complainant that, on 25.01.2018 at 7.00 AM, the accused has negligently left his dogs on Ayyappa Temple Road, Bairathi Village, to which they have all of sudden attacked CW.1, when he tried to escape, the said dogs followed CW.1 and harassed him.

It is further alleged that, accused came to the spot and when CW.1 enquired with him stating that, he should not leave the said dogs negligently on the road, to which the accused talked with CW.1 in high voice and also threatened with dire consequences.
Based on the typed complaint lodged by C.W.1, C.W.7 registered the case against accused in P.S. Crime No.14/2018 for the offence punishable under sections 506, 289 of IPC.
Investigating Officer/CW.7 investigated the matter, after completion of the investigation, has submitted final report against the accused for Offence punishable U/Secs. 289, 506 of IPC.
. Upon receipt of charge sheet, cognizance was taken for the above said offences alleged against the accused and registered the criminal case against him.
4. After registering the case, the accused has appeared and was enlarged on bail.
Copy of the charge sheet and its' enclosures were furnished to the accused in compliance of section 207 of Cr.P.C.
Sufficient grounds were made out to frame charges.
Hence, charges framed and read over to the accused.
He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

5. In order to prove the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has examined 03 witnesses out of 07 witnesses cited in the charge sheet as P.W.1 to P.W.3 and got marked 04 documents as per Ex.P.1 to V.Krishnappa vs John @ John Rogert on 14 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100274497/
2 Ex.P.4 and closed its side.
Thereafter, the accused was examined as provided U/s 313 of Cr.P.C by explaining incriminating evidence appearing against him.
The accused has denied the same and has not produced any oral or documentary evidence.
6. Heard both sides.
Perused the materials on record.

The points that arise for my consideration are;
1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on 25.01.2018 at 7.00 AM, the accused has negligently left the dogs in public road as to endanger the human life, under which CW.1 was walking on the said street, all of sudden, the said dogs attacked CW.1 and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.289 of IPC ?

2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on the above mentioned date,
time and place, accused has threatened CW.1 with dire consequences and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.506 of IPC ?
3. What Order?
8. My findings on the above points are as under:
Point Nos.1 and 2: In the Negative.
 Point No.3 : As per the final order  for the following;
 C.C.No.60156/2018  REASONS  9. POINT Nos.1 and 2:-
As these two points are interlinked, I have taken up these points together for common discussion to avoid repetition of facts & evidence.
In order to bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has to establish that,
the accused has negligently left the dogs in public road as to endanger the human life,
un- der which CW.1 was walking on the said street, all of sudden, the said dogs attacked CW.1 and when questioned, accused threatened CW.1 with dire consequences.

3 10.

In order to prove the above said allegations, the prosecution has examined the complainant/ victim/ CW.1 as PW.1, wherein, he has supported the case of the prosecution and deposed that, on 25.01.2018 at 7.00 PM, he was coming back from walking at Ayyappa Temple Road of Bairathi Vil- lage,
Two dogs followed him, he tried to escape, however, the said dogs barked at him and all of sudden attacked CW.1, to which he sustained scratched injuries on hand, legs and on body.
He has further deposed that, a person came over there C.C.No.60156/2018 and on enquiry he submitted that, he is the owner of the dogs and also threatened him with dire consequences.
PW.1 has further deposed that, by 1.00 PM, on the said day, he lodged complaint and the police authorities have conducted spot mahazar in his presence.

11. The prosecution has examined the independent witnesses i.e., CW.5 and 6 as PW.2 and 3,
wherein, they have partly supported the case of the prosecution and they have de- posed that, at 7.00 AM, they were coming back from walking at Ayyappa Temple road, CW.1 was attacked by the Dogs of the accused and CW.1 was taken to the hospital.
PW.2 and 3 have deposed that, due to the negligent act of the accused, the Dogs have attacked CW.1.

The learned Sr.APP have treated PW.2 and 3 as partly hostile, wherein, they have deposed re- garding the date of incident as on 25.01.2018 and also regard- ing the dire consequences given by the accused.
12. OVER ALL ANALYSIS :-
Before adverting to discuss on other aspects of the case, it would be appropriate to refer section 289 of IPC, which reads thus;
C.C.No.60156/2018 "289. Negligent conduct with respect to animal.
--Whoever knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with any animal in his posses- sion as is sufficient to guard against any proba- ble danger to human life, or any probable dan- ger of grievous hurt from such animal, shall be punished with imprisonment of either descrip- tion for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both."

13. The essential ingredients in order to constitute an offence U/s 289 of IPC are as follows;
i) The offence involves an animal.
ii) The accused must have acted negligently with respect to the animal.
iii) The negligent conduct must be likely to cause harm or injury to any person.
The negligent act of the accused must be culpable, which means it must be gross or of a nature that demonstrates a lack C.C.No.60156/2018 of concern for the safety of others.
The focus is on the likelihood of of harm not the actual harm.

Section 289 of IPC aims to address situations, where V.Krishnappa vs John @ John Rogert on 14 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100274497/
4
negligent handling of animals process risk to human safety.
14. Having gone through the essential ingredients of the offence U/s 289 of IPC, now let me consider the evidence led in by the prosecution.

On perusal of the materials on record, except the complainant and other eye witnesses i.e., CW.5 and 6, the prosecution has failed to secure the presence of panch mahazar witnesses I.e,, CW.2 and 3 and eye witness i.e., CW.4 and led their evidence.
More particularly, the prosecution has failed to secure and examine the investigating officer of the case.
It is well settled that, non-examination of the investigating officer is fatal to the case of prosecution.
15. I have carefully analyzed the ocular evidence of CW.1.
On perusal of complaint, which has been marked at Ex.P.1, the same has been addressed to the police inspector of the Kothanuru police Station by the Cw.1 from the office of Police Commissioner.
The incident has taken place in public place with regard to the complainant as alleged in personal capacity.
Therefore, in my considered opinion, the C.C.No.60156/2018 complainant ought to have filed the complaint in his personal capacity.
On perusal of the Ex.P.1, the complaint has been lodged on 25.01.2018 at 1.00 PM.
In comparison with the averments made in the complaint and the allegations by the prosecution, the incident took place on 25.01.2018 at 7.00 AM.
It has also come in the cross examination of PW.1 that the distance between the place of incident and the police station is of one kilometer.
If the incident had took place at 7.00 AM, even after attending the hospital, the complainant would have approached the police station and would have filed the complaint at the earliest.
On perusal of the Ex.P.1, it clearly fortifies that, the complainant has went to his office on the date of incident and got typed the complaint and thereafter, lodged the complaint.
It creates doubt on the case of the prosecution.

On perusal of the materials on record, the complainant has not intimated the fact of lodging the complaint to his higher authorities as the complaint has been addressed through the office of the complainant.
Therefore, it was incumbent on the part of the complainant to intimate his higher authorities.
16. On perusal of the ocular evidence of PW.2 and 3, they have partly supported the case of the prosecution and they C.C.No.60156/2018 have not deposed as to the date of the incident.
PW.2 has not deposed regarding the threat of life given by the accused to the CW.1.
PW.3 has identified the accused, but deposed that, he has seen the accused after the incident.
On perusal of examina- tion-in-chief of CW.5 and 6, they have more particularly deposed that, they have sent CW.1 to the hospital.
In compari- son with the contents of examination-in-chief of CW.1, he deposed that, he did not had any bleeding injuries, he did not take any medical treatment.
On perusal of the examination-in- chief of the PW.1 to 3, there are material discrepancies.
During the cross examination of PW.2, he admits that CW.1 had injuries on both the hands and body and pleaded ignorance as to who has taken CW.1 to the hospital.
On perusal of the cross examination of PW.3, he deposed that he don't know the contents of the statement and signed on the blank paper at the police station.
PW.3 has further admitted that, the dogs did not belonged to the accused and don't know the colour of the dogs.

17. I have carefully analyzed the cross examination of PW.1, wherein, it fortifies that, the accused has made effort in eliciting from the mouth of PW.1 that, earlier he worked as PI of Kothanuru Police V.Krishnappa vs John @ John Rogert on 14 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100274497/
5 Station, thereafter, by promotion he be- C.C.No.60156/2018 came ACP and by using the said power present complaint came to be filed.

sentences.text: Cross examination of PW.1 further fortifies that, he has admitted that, he has not given intimation to the higher authorities and also admitted that, the distance between the place of incident and the police station is about one kilo- meter.
Cross examination of PW.1 further reveals that, he has deposed that, he got scratch wounds on neck and hands.
The said averments is not being found either in the complaint or in the further statement.
On perusal of the cross examination of PW.1 in comparison with evidence of PW.2 and 3, there are material discrepancies.

18. Cross examination of PW.1 further fortifies that, the accused has taken defence that with regard to the food, there was quarrel between the stray dogs and pet dogs and the accused came in order to pacify the quarrel.
The accused has also taken defence that, the complainant by using his power as ACP has went on to assault CW.1.
However, there are no suf- ficient materials as to conclude that the accused has proved his defence.

Neverthless, in a case prosecuted and is being repre- sented by the State, it is the prosecution, who has to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt and the accused is not having any burden to prove his defence.
C.C.No.60156/2018 19.
On over all perusal of the materials on record, the prosecution has failed to substantiate the guilt of the accused by providing sufficient evidence.

The evidence on record, both by way of oral and documentary evidence are not sufficient to conclude that, the accused has negligently left the dogs under which they have attacked CW.1 and when enquired, accused gave life threats to CW.1.
Therefore, the prosecution has failed to substantiate the guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubt.
The ocular evidence of PW.1 to 3 in comparison with the documentary evidence are having material discrepancies with each other and are not sufficient to prove the guilt of the ac- cused.
In such circumstances, the prosecution has failed to es- tablish the guilt of the accused and benefit of doubt has to be extended to the accused and he is entitled for acquittal.
Ac- cordingly, the Point Nos.1 and 2 are answered in the "Neg- ative".
20. Point No.3:-

In view of the findings on above points, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER Acting under section 248(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused is acquitted of the offence punishable under C.C.No.60156/2018 sections 289, 506 of Indian Penal Code.
The personal bond of the  accused shall be in force for the  period of 6 months and thereafter  it shall be cancelled without  further orders.
